title: Verification Contract — Delivery Lifecycle Specification (ANVIL)
description: Machine-readable authority for the verification contract, corpus document 'verification-contract' (TS-013-04-02; human-readable counterpart TS-013-04-01). Encodes: gate semantics — verification is a lifecycle gate, mandatory and unskippable before a release may advance; a standard adds checks, it never weakens gates; an empty declaration leaves a no-op gate, not an open door (verification-contract.md §4, G1–G6; lifecycle-model.md §5.1) — and evidence requirements — evidence is the re-checkable output of a verification operation, a claim is not evidence; outcomes merge into the runtime's verification report and are recorded as lifecycle evidence (verification-contract.md §5, E1–E5). A verification declaration is what a standard declares as its verification content against this contract (verification-contract.md §6.2; ADR-033 §3): declared checks in the two contract categories (structural, lifecycle-conformity) bound to the two fixed gate positions (Verify stage, verify phase); the runtime invokes only declared capability (Manifesto §7; Transition Plan §5.9). Declarations that weaken gates and evidence that cannot be re-checked are rejected. Where this schema and verification-contract.md disagree, the schema governs (ADR-029 §3).
$comment: Dialect: draft-07, chosen for the widest validator support (python jsonschema, ajv, and mature independent implementations) — maximizing engine-path-independence per ADR-029 §3 and Transition Plan §5.10; no draft-2020-12-only feature is required. Version line (ADR-024 §3.1): the specification carries its own semver line decoupled from runtime releases; the contract major version is the unit of compatibility. This document is corpus version 1.0.0. A breaking change to this contract — any change to gate semantics or evidence requirements that breaks compatibility — is a governed event requiring an ADR and shipping with a Core major version (ADR-035 §3.1; verification-contract.md §2.4); specification artifacts publish via the spec/ tag line (ADR-024 §3.5). $id is a stable URN — it references the corpus document (verification-contract) on its version line and is independent of engine or repository paths; resolvable publication URL mechanics are EPIC-013 scope. Engine-path independence: this schema references no engine paths, no engine internals, and no standard content — a future re-home of the specification is a move, not a rewrite (ADR-029 §3; Transition Plan §5.2, §5.10). Concrete check declaration and evidence formats are deliberately not specified here: format-level decisions are deferred to EPIC-013 implementation design (verification-contract.md §6.3); this schema defines the declaration shape, not the formats.

$schema.description: Optional declaration of the schema this verification declaration targets (the $id of verification-contract.schema.json).

title.description: Optional human-readable title of the verification declaration.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the verification declaration.

id.description: Stable identifier of the verification declaration (the Verification part of a standard). Follows the corpus id convention: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens.

contractVersion.description: Target contract version of the delivery lifecycle specification (ADR-024 §3.1): semver, decoupled from runtime releases; major version is the compatibility unit. A declaration that targets an unsupported contract version is rejected by the runtime before any lifecycle operation.

gates.description: Gate semantics (verification-contract.md §4; G1–G6; PRD-002 §5.2–§5.3; Manifesto §3.2, §4.1): verification is a lifecycle gate, not an optional command. Each gate rule is encoded as a required const-true declaration — the gate set is a floor, not a ceiling; a declaration that omits a gate rule or asserts a weaker value is rejected (§4.4: content that weakens a gate is invalid; the machine-readable schema encodes this rejection).

verificationIsMandatory.description: G1: verification is mandatory — no lifecycle operation proceeds from unverified inputs; verification is a transition that cannot be skipped, not an optional command (Manifesto §3.2; PRD-002 §5.2–§5.3; lifecycle-model.md §6.2 R1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here weakens the gate and is rejected.

enforcedAsTransition.description: G2: gates are enforced, not requested — verification is enforced as a transition; the lifecycle cannot be bypassed; illegal transitions are rejected, not advised against (Manifesto §4.1; PRD-002 §5.2; lifecycle-model.md §6.2 R2). A declaration that asserts 'false' here weakens the gate and is rejected.

verificationPrecedesAdvancement.description: G3: verification precedes advancement — verification is mandatory before a release may advance, before any lifecycle operation consumes the artifact, and before the atomic promotion (Manifesto §3.2, §5.5; PRD-002 §5.3; artifact-manifest.md §5.1; lifecycle-model.md §5.1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here weakens the gate and is rejected.

standardAddsChecksNeverWeakensGates.description: G4: a standard adds checks; it never weakens gates — a standard declares verification content against this contract; it may not remove, skip, or relax a gate (007 §6; ADR-033 §3). The gate set is a floor, not a ceiling (§4.4); weakening a gate is a contract change — a governed event requiring an ADR, not a standard decision (ADR-035 §3.1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

allVerificationLayersMandatory.description: G5: all verification layers are mandatory — integrity, structural, and lifecycle-conformity verification are all gates; none may be skipped (artifact-manifest.md §5.2). A declaration that asserts 'false' here weakens the gate and is rejected.

failedVerificationRejectsOperation.description: G6: failed verification rejects the operation — an artifact that fails verification is rejected; no lifecycle operation proceeds from unverified inputs (artifact-manifest.md §5.3; PRD-002 §5.2). A gate that fails rejects the operation that violates it, it does not warn (verification-contract.md §1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

emptyDeclarationKeepsGate.description: §4.4 no-op gate nuance: declaring no content does not open the gate — a standard may declare zero verification checks; the gate position remains and the gate remains — a no-op gate, not an open door (lifecycle-model.md §5.1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here asserts the gate can be opened by declaring nothing and is rejected.

evidence.description: Evidence requirements (verification-contract.md §5; E1–E5; PRD-002 §5.3; Manifesto §3.2): evidence is embedded and re-checkable — a claim is not evidence; verification outcomes merge into the runtime's verification report and are recorded as lifecycle evidence. Each evidence rule is encoded as a required const-true declaration; a declaration that omits a rule or asserts a weaker value is rejected (E5: evidence that cannot be re-checked is invalid — the schema encodes this rejection).

claimIsNotEvidence.description: E1: a claim is not evidence — declaring a property is not proving it; evidence is the re-checkable output of a verification operation (PRD-002 §5.3; Manifesto §3.2). The artifact manifest contract demonstrates the distinction in concrete form: the manifest declares the expected hash — the claim; the verification operation recomputes the hash from the artifact's content and compares — the evidence (artifact-manifest.md §5.1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

evidenceIsRecheckable.description: E2: evidence is re-checkable — any consumer (the runtime, a CI pipeline, a human operator) can re-verify the same evidence; evidence is embedded and recorded, not held in the memory of the verifying process (Manifesto §3.2, §5.3; PRD-002 §5.3; artifact-manifest.md §5.1). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

outcomesMergeIntoVerificationReport.description: E3: outcomes merge into the runtime's verification report — verification outcomes are not left in the verifying process; they merge into the report the runtime keeps (007 §6). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

outcomesRecordedAsLifecycleEvidence.description: E4: outcomes are recorded as lifecycle evidence — part of the persisted, queryable, authoritative lifecycle state from which decisions derive (007 §6; PRD-002 §5.4; lifecycle-model.md §6.2 R8). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

nonRecheckableEvidenceIsInvalid.description: E5: evidence that cannot be re-checked is invalid — declarations whose evidence cannot be re-checked are rejected; the machine-readable schema encodes this rejection per check (checks[].evidence.recheckable must be true) (TS-013-04-02 §2; ADR-029 §3). A declaration that asserts 'false' here is rejected.

checks.description: Declared verification content (verification-contract.md §6.2; ADR-033 §3): the checks the standard declares as its verification content against this contract — declared capability. The runtime invokes only declared verification checks, at the declared positions; undeclared capability is never called (Manifesto §7; Transition Plan §5.9). Exactly the two contract categories may be declared — structural checks (the artifact contains what the framework requires: files, structures; the verified v1.x surface, preserved) and lifecycle-conformity checks (framework behavior at lifecycle points: shared-resource wiring, migration timing relative to promotion, queue restart, rollback behavior; the v2 verification depth). A check whose category the contract does not declare is undeclared capability and is rejected. The array may be empty: declaring no content does not open the gate — a no-op gate, not an open door (§4.4; lifecycle-model.md §5.1). Duplicated check declarations (deep equality) are rejected; id-based uniqueness is additionally enforced by the runtime at adoption.

id.description: Stable identifier of the declared check. Position bindings (positions.*.checks) and lifecycle definitions reference checks by id; the schema validates the id shape only — draft-07 cannot cross-validate id references between arrays, so id-to-declared-check resolution is additionally enforced by the runtime at adoption: undeclared capability is never called (Manifesto §7; Transition Plan §5.9).

category.description: The check category (verification-contract.md §6.2): 'structural' — the artifact contains what the framework requires (files, structures); the verified v1.x surface, preserved. 'lifecycle-conformity' — framework behavior at lifecycle points: shared-resource wiring, migration timing relative to promotion, queue restart, rollback behavior; the v2 verification depth. Exactly these two categories exist; any other category is capability this contract does not declare — e.g. integrity is owned by the artifact manifest contract (artifact-manifest.md §5), not standard content — and is rejected as undeclared capability.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of what this check verifies.

checkEvidence.description: Per-check evidence declaration (verification-contract.md §5; E2, E4, E5): what the check's outcome must be to count as evidence. A claim is not evidence (E1): the evidence declaration is a set of affirmations about the check's evidence, not a prose claim. Evidence that cannot be re-checked is invalid (E5) — a check whose evidence declaration omits an affirmation or asserts 'false' is rejected at declaration time.

recheckable.description: E2 / E5: the check's evidence is re-checkable — any consumer (the runtime, a CI pipeline, a human operator) can re-verify using the same evidence; evidence is embedded and recorded, not held in the memory of the verifying process (Manifesto §3.2, §5.3; artifact-manifest.md §5.1). 'false' is rejected: evidence that cannot be re-checked is invalid (E5).

embeddedOrRecorded.description: E2: the check's evidence is embedded in the artifact (e.g. a manifest entry) or recorded as lifecycle evidence — never held in the memory of the verifying process (Manifesto §5.3; verification-contract.md §5.2). 'false' is rejected.

recorded.description: E3 / E4: the check's outcome merges into the runtime's verification report and is recorded as lifecycle evidence — part of the persisted, queryable, authoritative lifecycle state from which decisions derive (007 §6; PRD-002 §5.4; lifecycle-model.md §6.2 R8). 'false' is rejected.

positions.description: Position bindings (verification-contract.md §4.2): where the declared checks execute. The gate positions are fixed by the specification; a standard supplies content within the defined lifecycle — it does not invent gates or move gate positions (Manifesto §3.1; 007 §5). Exactly the two contract positions may be declared: the Verify stage (artifact lifecycle — before any lifecycle operation may consume the artifact; structural and lifecycle-conformity verification follow the integrity gate, artifact-manifest.md §5.2) and the verify phase (activation sequence — the fixed contract-level position immediately before the atomic promotion, lifecycle-model.md §5.1). A binding may declare zero checks: the phase is a no-op gate, not an open door (§4.4; lifecycle-model.md §5.1).

verifyStage.description: Checks bound to the Verify stage (artifact lifecycle): structural and lifecycle-conformity verification executed after the integrity gate passes (artifact-manifest.md §5.2). May be empty — the integrity gate belongs to the artifact manifest contract and remains.

verifyPhase.description: Checks bound to the verify phase (activation sequence): activation-time verification content at the fixed contract-level position immediately before the atomic promotion (lifecycle-model.md §5.1). May be empty — a no-op gate, not an open door (§4.4).

checks.description: Declared checks bound to this position, referenced by id (see checks[].id). May be empty — a no-op gate, not an open door (§4.4; lifecycle-model.md §5.1). The schema validates the id shape only; id-to-declared-check resolution is enforced by the runtime at adoption — undeclared capability is never called (Manifesto §7; Transition Plan §5.9).
